title: Secretary of State of Michigan

context.text: The seat is open: Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson cannot run for reelection. The Michigan Bureau of Elections' candidate listing for the November 3, 2026 general election names five candidates: Garlin Gilchrist II (Democratic), Anthony Forlini (Republican), Eric Borregard (Green), Christine Sloan (Libertarian) and Scott Aughney (U.S. Taxpayers).

All five were nominated at party conventions rather than a primary; the state listing records filing dates of August 31, 2026 for Gilchrist, August 24 for Forlini, July 20 for Aughney, June 29 for Sloan and February 23 for Borregard.

candidates.name: Garlin Gilchrist II
candidates.ballotNote: Democratic Party nominee; filed August 31, 2026 following the party convention (Michigan Bureau of Elections listing).

summary.text: Garlin Gilchrist is the Democratic nominee for Michigan Secretary of State and has been lieutenant governor since 2019. A computer engineer by training, he left the race for governor in January 2026 to run for this office, and is campaigning on protecting voter data from federal access, campaign-finance transparency and better Secretary of State branch services.

background.text: Lieutenant Governor of Michigan since 2019, serving with Gov. Gretchen Whitmer.
Previously a computer engineer; ran unsuccessfully for Detroit city clerk in 2017 against incumbent Janice Winfrey.
Entered the Secretary of State race in January 2026 after dropping out of the race for governor.

priorities.text: Protecting Michigan voters' data from federal access; he said he would not turn over the unredacted voter roll to the Justice Department.
Campaign-finance transparency, including disclosure of dark-money donors before an election and 'real-time enforcement' of violations, under a plan he calls 'Stand TALL.'
Modernizing licensing and registration services and holding repair companies that overcharge customers accountable.

positions.summary: His campaign site lists protecting abortion access among his accomplishments working alongside Gov. Whitmer.

statements.quote: As a process person, I want to make sure that we get that number to zero. I also want to make sure that we are focusing on the right things, and that is again making sure we have a good process,
statements.context: Asked about requiring proof of citizenship to register; he said voting is reserved for citizens and that "vanishingly few noncitizens … actually cast ballots"

record.text: Lieutenant governor in the Whitmer administration; his campaign says he played a leading role in free pre-K for all, abortion-access protections and expanded internet connectivity.

candidates.researchNotes: Record is the campaign's description of his role; no legislative or executive documents were loaded.

candidates.name: Anthony Forlini
candidates.ballotNote: Republican Party nominee; filed August 24, 2026 following the party convention (Michigan Bureau of Elections listing).

summary.text: Anthony Forlini is the Republican nominee for Michigan Secretary of State and has been Macomb County clerk since 2021. A former Harrison Township supervisor and state representative, he is campaigning on cleaner voter rolls, shorter Secretary of State wait times and more election transparency.

background.text: Harrison Township supervisor before serving in the Michigan House of Representatives from 2011 to 2016.
Ran for Michigan's 10th Congressional District in 2016, finishing fourth of five in the Republican primary.
Elected Macomb County clerk in 2020 and re-elected in 2024.

priorities.text: Keeping voter rolls clean: using public databases to remove ineligible voters, removing deceased voters, and referring multiple voters for prosecution.
Cutting Secretary of State office wait times and having real people answer the phone; auditing county clerks for consistency.
Election transparency, including retaining more election data such as electronic pollbook records.

statements.context: Votebeat's paraphrase and quote: asked about requiring proof of citizenship, Forlini said self-reported citizenship is not enough and the government 'has some responsibility' to verify it

record.text: As Macomb County clerk, introduced an online tool that posts images of every ballot cast for public viewing after an election.

Compared Macomb County's voter rolls with the jury pool to look for noncitizens; the effort flagged 15 voters, and the Michigan Department of State later said five appeared to be noncitizens and at least three were citizens.

candidates.researchNotes: Michigan House voting record 2011-2016 was not reviewed. Statement entry is a fragment because Votebeat paraphrased the rest of his answer.
